title: Estás en tu casa
subtitle: Settling in before dinner
scene: You’re inside. {mom} is finishing dinner and {dad} offers you a drink.

culture.title: Mi casa es tu casa
culture.text: It’s a real welcome, not a cliché. Accept it warmly, but still ask before helping yourself to things.

lines.es: Muchas gracias. Su casa es muy bonita.
lines.en: Thank you so much. Your house is very pretty.
lines.note: Su casa = your house (usted). With {sibling} it would be tu casa.

lines.es: ¿Quieres algo de tomar? ¿Un refresco? ¿Agua de jamaica?
lines.en: Do you want something to drink? A soda? Hibiscus water?
lines.note: In Mexico, tomar is the everyday verb for “to drink”.

lines.es: Un agua de jamaica, por favor.
lines.note: Agua is feminine, but it takes un: un agua, el agua.

lines.es: Yo la traigo. ¡Mi mamá la hace muy rica!
lines.en: I’ll bring it. My mom makes it really good!

la.n: La replaces agua: yo la traigo = I’ll bring it.

lines.es: Siéntate, {me}. La cena está casi lista.
lines.en: Sit down, {me}. Dinner is almost ready.
lines.note: Siéntate = sit down (tú). To an elder you’d say siéntese.

lines.en: Can I help you with anything, ma’am?

culture.title: Ofrecer ayuda
culture.text: Offering to help is good manners, even if the answer is no. Hosts often say no the first time.
